features: 【Specification】18 Gauge 8 conductor wire(Red & Black & Yellow & White). Black PVC Jacket. 50ft/15M. Maximum input voltage: 300V(also can for DC5V/12V/24V). Maximum current: 7.5A. Rated working temperature up to 80℃/176℉

【8 Conductor Tinned Copper Wire】Our 18 AWG 8 wire cable consists of 34 strands of 0.2mm tinned copper wire inside each cable. The tin coating not only enhances conductivity, but also provides excellent resistance to corrosion and oxidation. Compared to ordinary copper wire, it greatly extends the service life of the power cable. It is also more suitable for soldering, making it a reliable choice

【PVC Durable Material】The jacket of our 8 core extension wire is made of high quality PVC, providing protection against wear and tear in harsh environments. It offers numerous advantages, including flame retardancy, high compressive strength, resistance to aging, acid and alkali, and excellent corrosion performance. Whether buried directly or exposed to sunlight for prolonged periods, it remains durable and reliable.

【Easy to Use】Our 8 conductor tinned copper wire is flexible for easy connection, stripping, and soldering. The high quality PVC insulation is safe for use in walls. This versatile wire is widely used in various applications such as lamps, automobiles, relays, model airplanes or cars, ships, motor leads, digital fields, LED strips, and inverter wiring. It is also suitable for security systems, alarm systems, access control, speaker audio, thermostat cables, and more.

【Quality assurance】Customer satisfaction is our top priority. We take pride in our wire, which goes through excellent production processes, ensuring low eccentricity and a uniform thickness PVC jacket that prevents current breakdown and ignition. We offer a two-year warranty, and if you experience any inconvenience within this period, please do not hesitate to contact us. Our dedicated team will resolve any issues within 24 hours.

Nice highly flexible 18 gage wire. It is tinned, so if you plan to solder, that is even better. I am using this as a signal wire from remote/pendant mounted switches to control small relays. For this, it is well suited, possibly a little overkill. But I like having a little heavier gage than what it takes just to get the job done. In my experience, it lasts longer and more forgiving to unexpected issues and faults.The outer sheath is not terribly difficult to cut, but I do not think average use will cause damage to it. Probably not suited to use in a manufacturing plant where it would be subjected to many types of abuse. But for the average DIY home entrepreneur, it would likely be just fine. I think we all take better care of things when it is us who foot the bill to pay for them.The individual wires are color coded (think thermostat wire), so they are easily identifiable on each end. As mentioned they are tinned, so the are easily soldered as well. I like soldered connections. They are more trouble to install, but, when properly done, I feel they are extremely reliable and with lower resistance due to more surface contact area. Soldering is not always an option, but these wires will do just fine when crimped as well.

top_reviews.review_title: Excellent cable, a bit overkill for thermostat
top_reviews.review_text:
This is a very good cable, perhaps overkill for thermostat wire.It has 8 conductors and a very thick PVC jacket.The strands are of tinned copper (See image where I scratched off the tin coat).Colors on the strands: White, Black, Red, Blue, Green, Orange, Yellow, Brown.There is plenty of chalk when removing the outer sleeve. Chalk is used to keep moisture out, which makes it less combustible. It's not riser rated though.Marking on the cable:ESHENG PAI STYLE2497435P 2464 18AWG 80ºC 300V VW-I 1 A 18AWG 80ºC 300V PTI TRIUMPHCABLESo, a legit, good quality Triumph Wire (China) cable sold under a seemingly random name.It's exactly as described on the listing.Keep in mind that this is stranded wire and the jacket is a bit thick. It's very flexible, so it does work as a thermostat wire although overkill. Because it's stranded, it's not as quick working on it as a solid wire.So not ideal as a thermostat cable, but a quality cable regardless.
